title: HP OmniBook Ultra 14 (2026) review: thin, fast and expensive
metaDescription: Our HP OmniBook Ultra 14 (2026) review: Snapdragon X2 Elite or Intel Panther Lake, the 3K OLED, battery life, the new keyboard and missing USB-A port.
excerpt: HP's slimmest premium laptop comes with a 3K OLED and a choice of Snapdragon X2 Elite or Intel chips. The price is high, and the new keyboard will not suit everyone.
_note: Research review built from published testing. If you test it yourself, add measurements and rewrite How we tested.

image.alt: HP OmniBook Ultra 14 (2026) laptop open, showing the 3K OLED screen and keyboard

verdict.summary: The OmniBook Ultra 14 is one of the thinnest and best-looking Windows laptops of 2026, with a sharp 120Hz OLED and a choice of Snapdragon or Intel chips. The Snapdragon model is the better value if your apps run on Arm. But the price climbs past $2,000 quickly, there is no USB-A or SD slot, and the new keyboard is softer than the one it replaces.
bestFor: People who want a very thin and light Windows laptop with an OLED touchscreen
Snapdragon buyers whose apps all run on Arm
skipIf: You need USB-A or an SD card slot without dongles
You rely on older Windows software that may not run on Arm

pros.text: Snapdragon model is cheaper than a comparable Intel model

cons.text: Keyboard is spongier than the 2024 model
cons.evidence: Notebookcheck found it spongier with shallower travel

cons.text: No USB-A port or SD card reader
Expensive, at $2,000 or more for the well-equipped models

sections.heading: What the OmniBook Ultra 14 is
sections.body:
HP's OmniBook Ultra 14 for 2026 launched at CES 2026 and is the first HP laptop with Qualcomm's Snapdragon X2 Elite chip (Windows Central). It is also sold with Intel Core Ultra Series 3 Panther Lake processors.

Windows Central reported the Snapdragon model at $2,049.99 at Best Buy as an introductory price, with the Intel model starting at $1,699.99 from HP.

sections.heading: How we tested it
sections.body:
We have not tested the OmniBook Ultra 14 ourselves. This review brings together reporting and testing from Windows Central, IBTimes Australia and Notebookcheck. Every figure on this page names where it came from. No source we read had independently measured battery life or display brightness.

When we get a unit, we will add our own battery and performance results here and update the verdict.

sections.heading: Snapdragon or Intel?
sections.body:
The Snapdragon X2 Elite is an Arm chip, so check that your key apps and drivers run on Windows on Arm. The Intel version gives the widest compatibility and Thunderbolt 4. Windows Central found the Snapdragon model about $290 cheaper than an Intel model with similar memory and storage.

For most people the Snapdragon model is the better buy, as long as nothing you rely on needs an x86 driver. Choose Intel if you use specialist software, older games or Thunderbolt docks.

sections.heading: Design and display
sections.body:
The aluminum body is 0.42 inches thick and weighs about 2.8lb. HP rates the 3K OLED at about 500 nits in standard mode and 1,100 nits in HDR. There is no USB-A port, a first for the OmniBook line (Notebookcheck), and no SD card reader.

This is the strongest part of the laptop. It is light enough to carry all day, and the 120Hz OLED gives it an edge over many rivals at this price.

sections.heading: Battery and performance
sections.body:
HP claims up to 44 hours of battery life, measured under its own test conditions. IBTimes Australia reported Cinebench 2026 scores of 4,646 multi-core and 632 single-core for the Snapdragon model, and found it handled 4K video editing without problems.

Treat the 44-hour figure as a best case. No independent battery test was available when we wrote this, so we cannot say how close real use gets.

sections.heading: Keyboard
sections.body:
Notebookcheck's main complaint is the redesigned keyboard, which it found spongier and shallower than the 2024 model's. IBTimes Australia reported more positive impressions, so try one in a store if you can.

If you type for a living, try it before you buy.

sections.heading: Should you buy the OmniBook Ultra 14?
sections.body:
It suits people who want a very thin Windows laptop with an OLED touchscreen and can afford the premium. Choose the Snapdragon model for value if your apps run on Arm, and the Intel model for compatibility and Thunderbolt.

The OmniBook Ultra 14 is a very good laptop at a high price.

alternatives.name: Dell XPS 14 (2026)
alternatives.why: Similar price with strong Intel Arc graphics and a classic XPS design.

alternatives.name: Apple MacBook Air
alternatives.why: Thinner, fanless and cheaper, if you do not need Windows or a touchscreen.

faq.q: How much does the HP OmniBook Ultra 14 (2026) cost?
faq.a: Windows Central reported $1,699.99 for the Intel base model at HP and $2,049.99 for the Snapdragon X2 Elite model at Best Buy. Prices vary by configuration and retailer.

faq.q: Does the HP OmniBook Ultra 14 have a USB-A port?
faq.a: No. It has three USB-C ports (Thunderbolt 4 on Intel, USB4 on Snapdragon) and a headphone jack, so you need an adapter for USB-A devices.
